question: Which of the following imaging modalities does NOT use ionising radiation?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Fluoroscopy uses continuous X-ray beams — an ionising modality — to produce real-time images.
CT uses multiple X-ray projections reconstructed into cross-sectional images and is an ionising modality, typically with higher doses than plain radiography.
Nuclear medicine uses radionuclides that emit ionising gamma or positron radiation detected externally.
Correct. Ultrasound uses high-frequency sound waves — a non-ionising modality — making it safe in pregnancy and paediatric patients without radiation risk.

overallFeedback.feedback: Not quite. Ultrasound and MRI are the non-ionising modalities; X-ray, fluoroscopy, CT, and nuclear medicine all use ionising radiation.
Correct! Diagnostic ultrasound and MRI are the two non-ionising modalities in the standard imaging toolkit.
